discovery: Invention of the high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) and its realisation in AlGaN/GaN heterostructures

nominees.name: Umesh K. Mishra
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Santa Barbara, USA

motivation: In 1979-80 Takashi Mimura invented the high-electron-mobility transistor. It uses a two-dimensional electron gas at a modulation-doped heterointerface, where electrons move without scattering from their donor impurities. The HEMT became the low-noise amplifier in satellite receivers, radio telescopes and mobile networks. In 1993 Asif Khan demonstrated the first AlGaN/GaN HEMT, in which polarization fields form a dense 2DEG without any intentional doping. Umesh Mishra turned this physics into reliable high-power, high-frequency GaN transistors. Today GaN HEMTs drive 5G base stations, radar and compact, highly efficient power converters, and they cut the electricity lost in power conversion worldwide. This work shows how understanding heterointerface physics and crystal quality leads to transistors that save energy and serve society.
